- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction.
- Model shows persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment reversal.
- In 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce noise in forecast tails.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day prices for correction.
